article_title: Effectiveness of Using GeoGebra on Students' Understanding in Learning Circles
citation: Shadaan, P., & Leong, K. E. (2013). Effectiveness of Using Geogebra on Students' Understanding in Learning Circles. The Malaysian Online Journal of Educational Technology, 1(4). https://www.mojet.net
title: T2S4VU conceptual framework linking technology, self-exploration and social interaction to visualization and understanding
description: The T2S4VU framework organizes the study's GeoGebra intervention around five components: T = Technology, where "the GeoGebra software is an important scaffold to bridge the ZPD"; S = Self-exploration, a central constructivist concept; S = Social interaction, allowing learners to interact with peers and knowledgeable others; V = Visualization; and U = Understanding. It is grounded in Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and scaffolding, with the teacher acting as facilitator.
requirements: Students work in pairs constructing diagrams so peer scaffolding can occur, with input from both group members balanced
constraints: The process had to be closely monitored to ensure a balance in terms of input from both group members
target_learners: Year 9 (Form 3) secondary mathematics students of varied abilities
target_learning_goals: Understanding of circle concepts through visualization and exploration
examples: Students worked in pairs to construct circle diagrams in GeoGebra and made conjectures based on their constructions, with teacher and peers acting as additional scaffolds
key_sources: Shadaan, P., & Leong, K. E. (2013). Effectiveness of Using Geogebra on Students' Understanding in Learning Circles. The Malaysian Online Journal of Educational Technology, 1(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1086434
